correctness.rationale: Let b_m=chi(overline M_{0,m+1}), with b_2=1. From Getzler–McMullen inversion and chi(M_{0,n+1})=(-1)^n(n-2)! the formal inverse is f(x)=2x-(1+x)log(1+x). Writing g=f^{-1}=x+h and differentiating yields h'=x+2h+hh', so b_{m+1}=2b_m+sum_{k=2}^{m-1}binom(m,k)b_k b_{m-k+1}. A complete parity-split induction modulo 4 proves b_{2r}=(-1)^{r+1} mod4, b_{2r+1}=2 mod4. Even-row binomial parity follows Lucas; the odd-row contribution uses the exact sum of its even binomial coefficients. Translating m=n-1 gives chi(overline M_{0,n}) mod4 = 1,2,3,2 for n congruent 3,0,1,2 mod4. Independent rational EGF composition checked to order 20 and full integer recurrence residues through b_70. The open spaces are not substituted for the compactified ones.
residual_risks: Proof assumes n>=3, i.e. stable pointed rational curves; does not claim individual Betti-number residues.
Finite recurrence verification alone is not all-n proof; the separately reconstructed modular induction is required.

originality.rationale: Getzler/McMullen already establish the compactified Euler inverse-series relationship and its first numerical values. Aluffi–Marcolli–Nascimento 2025 Section 8 gives the same Euler differential equation, Lambert-W expression and Stirling-coefficient formulas, but no complete mod-four valuation classification. Goulden–Litsyn–Shevelev 2005 and Drake–Gessel–Xin 2007 analyze the identical sequence, its quadratic recurrence and Laurent-polynomial auxiliary coefficients, respectively; neither materially read statement is an all-n chi modulo four classification. Official OEIS A074059 has the functional equation and recurrence without such a rule. Exact equivalence, broader coverage, and same-sequence alternate notation were checked. Prior derivations furnish starting identities, not the asserted congruence induction. Best-of-knowledge, not a guarantee against older obscure integer-sequence congruences.
residual_risks: Classical Lagrange-inversion, Ward-number, and sequence congruence sources not indexed under the geometric name might contain the mod-four law.
The general exact Stirling formulas, while not stating this result, could give a short alternative proof; this does not itself negate independent mathematical significance.

value.rationale: The Euler characteristic of every compactified genus-zero pointed moduli space is a canonical topological invariant. The theorem determines its complete two-primary behavior: it is never divisible by four and even-index values have exact valuation one. The all-size periodic residue pattern is not a restatement of a known numerical table and connects geometric stratification to Lucas parity; a self-contained natural infinite classification is mathematically valuable.
residual_risks: No new geometric Betti-number theorem or higher-adic valuation is claimed.

limitations: n>=3 stable pointed genus-zero compactification only.
The exact congruence is a formal consequence of known inversion machinery but was not identified as a previously stated theorem.
